Enterprise AI startup AidenAI has raised $32 Mn (₹297.1 Cr) in a Series A funding round led by growth investment firm A91 Partners, as it looks to expand its AI platform and engineering capabilities. The fresh capital will be used to invest in its platform and engineering talent as it looks to scale its global enterprise AI business. “With A91 as our partner, we are excited to invest in our people and platforms and help shape the next wave of enterprise technology services,” AidenAI founder and CEO Srinivas Kamadi said. Kamadi founded AidenAI in 2023 after spending nearly two decades with Infosys. Drawing on his experience of leading digital transformation at the company, Kamadi launched AidenAI to solve a recurring bottleneck faced by large enterprises: enterprise AI was stuck in the experimentation phase because outdated legacy systems made digital transformation too slow. The New Jersey-based startup, whose majority of workforce is based out of Hyderabad, helps large enterprises integrate AI into existing applications, data infrastructure and business workflows. Its proprietary AI Builder Platform is designed to help businesses move beyond AI experimentation and deploy AI applications within their existing tech infrastructure. This platform connects with an enterprise’s existing systems and AI models, providing tools for AI agents. The startup also offers AiDAP, an AI-driven technology modernisation platform that helps enterprises modernise legacy software systems. This positions AidenAI in the enterprise AI implementation market, where businesses are increasingly looking for solutions to integrate AI into business-critical operations rather than deploy standalone tools. “While enterprise AI adoption is still in its early stages, AidenAI has spent the last 3 years helping over 30 large enterprises turn the promise of AI into live, measurable business outcomes,” said A91 Partners’ partner Kaushik Anand. Alongside its platform expansion, AidenAI plans to build a team of more than 1,000 frontier AI engineers through its AidenAI Builder Academy. The academy is designed to develop forward-deployed engineering talent that can work directly with enterprise clients to build and deploy production-ready AI applications using the company’s platform and frontier AI models. The expansion comes as enterprises increasingly explore agentic AI applications to automate complex, multi-step workflows across functions such as finance, insurance, healthcare and human resources. AidenAI aims to tap this demand by combining AI agents, enterprise software modernisation and specialised engineering services. This comes as the broader Indian enterprise AI market, which was valued at $11 Bn in 2025, is projected to reach $71 Bn by 2030, according to Inc42’s Bharat AI Startups Report 2026. As more companies adopt GenAI in their daily operations, demand is growing for providers that can build and deploy AI solutions at an enterprise scale. AidenAI is positioning itself at this intersection via its AI Builder Platform and engineering-led deployment model. Its presence across six countries and a client base of over 30 enterprises provide an early indication of market traction. However, the startup’s ability to scale will depend on how effectively it can standardise its platform across enterprise customers with different technology infrastructure and business requirements.
